explanation:
I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem says that the ideal-primary component `Ideal.primaryComponent G (span {(p : ℤ)})` and the `p`-primary subgroup `AddCommGroup.primaryComponent G p` have the same members. The ideal comes from `integerPrime`, which the library defines itself, so that part of the statement is not Mathlib's.

What I searched:
- All of Mathlib for `primaryComponent`, `Ideal.primaryComponent` and `integerPrime`.
- `Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Torsion/PrimaryComponent.lean`, which has `primaryComponent_mem`, `.map`, `map_surjective`, `iSup_primaryComponent_eq_top` and `iSupIndep_primaryComponent`.
- `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Torsion.lean`, which has `primaryComponent` and `mem_primaryComponent`.

Neither file relates the ideal-primary component of a ℤ-module to the group-theoretic `p`-primary subgroup. The current proof works from the two membership characterisations (`Ideal.primaryComponent_mem`, `mem_primaryComponent`) and adds a short argument about the span of `p` and the integer action. That argument is more than routine glue, so I don't count this as a special case of either lemma.
